dossier.public_summary: A 1008 ppm dip at 12.8 days looks planetary in duration and size but earths differ strongly between sectors (1196 to 588 ppm) and between individual transits (180 to 1723 ppm). A secondary eclipse at 23% the primary depth and a grazing V-shaped transit point to a blended stellar eclipsing binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth truly changes between sectors/products (82.32% change) much larger than errors, not a calibration offset.
reasons.value: changes_within_a_source: 1196 (SPOC 2-min, sector 10) vs 1485 (TESS-SPOC, sector 63) vs 588 (QLP, sector 90), p_constant 1.8514450857768983e-06

reasons.why: Individual transits are inconsistent; one transit is far too shallow and one extremely deep, inconsistent with a planet.
reasons.value: chi2 71.28 dof 4 p_consistent 1.22e-14, outliers depth 180 ppm sigma -5.7 and 1723 ppm sigma 5.0, share_of_top_3 0.924

reasons.why: Significant secondary eclipse at 36% phase seen in the same data set as the primary, favours a stellar companion with self-occultation over a planet.

reasons.why: High V-shape and grazing geometry support a grazing eclipsing binary; flat bottom not seen.
